title: Bass players and stance
summary: He explains what he wants from bassists and why they should stand up.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And is it something you can actually tell a bass player.

No. You can’t. It’s where he hears the time. The one thing that I do on most occasions — the thing that bothers me the most is okay you get to the gig and you see the bass player there and the hatchback’s opening up and the first thing I see that comes out of the hatchback is the stool. I say that’s a stand-up bass. Stand on your two feet and play it man, you know because you’re anchored. For instance, like Miles Davis used to tell guys, you don’t play like with the front part of your foot. I mean that’s not anchored. You’ve got to stand up. When you see Paul Chambers or any of these guys play you see their heel like this [plays bass]. Not like [plays bass]. I mean you’re off balance. It’s got to be like — Miles had to tell the guys play it. It’s your spine to the heel [plays bass]. You see?

So when I see a guy sitting down, his feet aren’t even on the floor, half the time they’re up on the thing, what are you playing with? It’s coming from your head to your fingers. It’s supposed to come right straight through your body. For me.
